North Carolina, single, 2026: gross $92,000.00 a year ($3,538.46 biweekly). Federal income tax $10,195.60 on taxable income $70,380.00 after the $16,100.00 standard deduction (marginal 22%). Social Security $5,704.00 (6.2% up to the $184,500.00 wage base), Medicare $1,334.00. State income tax $2,941.83 (exact 2026 schedule). Take-home $66,304.57 a year, $2,550.18 per biweekly paycheck; effective tax rate 21.93%.

Estimate of annual tax on wages, not tax advice and not your employer's W-4 withholding. Uses the standard deduction and no credits. Local taxes (NYC, Yonkers, Ohio cities, Pennsylvania EIT, Maryland and Indiana counties) and state payroll taxes such as CA SDI are not included.

steps: NC base $86,480 (federal AGI: wages minus 401(k) and HSA) minus the $12,750 standard deduction = $73,730 x 3.99% = $2,941.83.
notes: Flat 3.99% for tax years after 2025, after the standard deduction ($12,750 single and separate, $25,500 joint, $19,125 head of household; NC-30 2026).
Married filing separately gets $0 standard deduction if the spouse itemizes; that case is not modeled.

assumptions: Annual liability for tax year 2026, spread evenly over 26 pay periods. Your employer's withholding (IRS Pub. 15-T, W-4) can differ.
This pay is treated as the household's only income, with the standard deduction and no credits or other adjustments.

401(k) is a traditional pre-tax deferral: it lowers income tax but not Social Security or Medicare. HSA is a payroll (cafeteria plan) contribution: it lowers income tax, Social Security and Medicare (IRS Pub. 15-B).
Additional Medicare tax uses the single threshold of $200,000. Employers withhold it on wages over $200,000 regardless of filing status; the difference settles on Form 8959.

Income tax is computed from the rate schedules. The IRS Tax Table (taxable income under $100,000) and New York's tax table (under $65,000) use $50 bands, so a filed return can differ by a few dollars.
Local income taxes are out of scope.
